proposals.announcement_evidence: for active electronically scanned array radars of Air Force F-16 aircraft
proposals.lexicon_quote: Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) | F01600 | 407 | F-16 Modifications
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the lexicon row's name verbatim (case-insensitively) minus its parenthetical acronym: 'active electronically scanned array radars of Air Force F-16 aircraft'. The action is a retrofit of AESA radars onto fielded USAF F-16s, and the money obligated is overwhelmingly Aircraft Procurement (fiscal 2023 aircraft procurement $21,879,678 plus fiscal 2022 aircraft procurement $275,xxx, against $7,794,677 of aircraft RDT&E), which is the appropriation F01600 (doc 407, Aircraft Procurement) sits in; F-16 Modifications is precisely the procurement line that buys and installs F-16 modification kits, and its own J-book narrative owns the AESA name. Flagged for lens B: the identical name 'Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA)' also appears under F0160P (F-16 Post Production Support, doc 407) — I chose F01600 because installing a new radar on in-service aircraft is a modification, not post-production support of an existing configuration, but the collision is real and lens B should test it.

refute_a.reason: Money color holds: the obligation is dominated by aircraft procurement (FY23 $21,879,678 plus FY22 $275,xxx, against $7,794,677 RDT&E) and F01600's account is Aircraft Procurement, Air Force — the line that buys and installs F-16 AESA mod kits; the matched name is the radar, not the F-16 platform, and 'F-16 Modifications' is a specific mod line, not a CATCHALL_TITLE rollup.

refute_b.reason: The identical name 'Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA)' is owned verbatim by F0160P (F-16 Post Production Support, doc 407) as well as F01600, and the quoted evidence ('active electronically scanned array radars of Air Force F-16 aircraft') contains nothing that selects modification over post-production support; worse, this same contract FA8615-17-C-6047 and the same wording are used in this chunk (record 53) to link 0207133F, so one evidence string is linking three PEs — the disambiguation rests entirely on appropriation reasoning, not on identity.

proposals.announcement_evidence: in firm-fixed-price task orders under the National Security Space Launch Phase 2 contract
proposals.lexicon_quote: The National Security Space Launch (NSSL) | NSSL00 | 416 | National Security Space Launch
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the program verbatim — the task orders are issued under the National Security Space Launch Phase 2 contract itself, not under a vehicle that merely touches NSSL. The obligated money is fiscal 2020 missile procurement ($7,307,274) and fiscal 2020 space procurement ($22,336,293), i.e. procurement appropriations, which matches NSSL00 at doc 416 (Space/procurement) rather than the RDT&E EMD line 1206853SF that carries the same name at doc 417. Early integration studies and fleet surveillance are the recurring launch-service work this procurement line buys. Flagged for lens B: the name collides with 1206853SF (National Security Space Launch Program (SPACE) - EMD); the appropriation cited in the announcement is what separates them.

refute_a.reason: Both obligated tranches are procurement (FY20 missile procurement $7,307,274 + FY20 space procurement $22,336,293) against NSSL00, whose account is Procurement, Space Force — the successor of exactly those AF missile/space procurement accounts — and early integration studies plus fleet surveillance are launch-service support the NSSL line itself buys, so there is no O&M-on-procurement mismatch, no platform substitution (NSSL is the program) and no rollup.

refute_b.reason: 'The National Security Space Launch (NSSL)' is an exact-name row at BOTH NSSL00 (doc 416) and 1206853SF (doc 417, NSSL Program (SPACE) - EMD), and the only evidence offered is the vehicle name 'National Security Space Launch Phase 2 contract', which both rows own verbatim; the described work ('early integration studies and fleet surveillance for non-national security space missions') reads as development-side effort and is explicitly for non-NSS missions, so the identity of which NSSL line owns it is genuinely ambiguous.

refute_a.reason: Exact appropriation match — Air Force fiscal 2016/2017 ammunition procurement against 356010 (Procurement of Ammunition, Air Force) — and the contract is the outright purchase of the MJU-66/B flare, the end item the Expendable Countermeasures line funds, so nothing is a platform the award merely supports; the concurrent Navy ammunition tranche does not displace the AF line's own work, and the IDIQ names its program so §3's umbrella reject does not apply.

refute_b.reason: 'MJU-66' appears at exactly one pe_bli in the F index (356010, Expendable Countermeasures, doc 409); MJU-66/B is the ordinary mod-letter form of the same item, not a different increment, the sibling rows MJU-52A/61/62/64/73/75 sit on the same line, and the evidence is the item designator itself rather than a contractor name — no alternative owner exists to break it on.

proposals.announcement_evidence: to exercise the option for Lot 11 production of joint programmable fuze systems
proposals.rationale: The Joint Programmable Fuze is the FMU-152A/B, and the announcement's own contractor corroborates the identity: Kaman Precision Products of Orlando, Florida is the JPF producer, the award is a Lot 11 production option for 7,846 fuze systems, and the contracting activity is AFLCMC at Eglin — the JPF program office. refute_a.reason: Fiscal 2014/2015 ammunition procurement funds against 356120 (Procurement of Ammunition, Air Force) is an exact money-color match, and the Lot 11 option is a production buy of 7,846 fuze systems — the itemized end item, not services, sustainment or a platform — with 'Fuzes' an itemized commodity line rather than a CATCHALL_TITLE aggregate.

refute_b.reason: 'FMU-152A' is unique to 356120 in the F index, the JPF alias is real (Kaman Precision Products, Orlando, Lot 11 production at AFLCMC Eglin is the Joint Programmable Fuze program), and even the only competing designator reading of 'joint programmable fuze' — the FMU-139C/D rows — sits at the SAME pe_bli 356120, so no other PE in the index owns this evidence; no index row carries 'programmable' as a program name elsewhere.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for Active Electronically Scanned Array radars of Air Force F-16 aircraft. This modification is for continued radar development.
proposals.lexicon_quote: APG-83 | 0207133F | 412 | F-16 Squadrons
proposals.rationale: The Northrop Grumman AESA radar for the USAF F-16 on contract FA8615-17-C-6047 is the AN/APG-83 SABR — the announcement uses the capability description rather than the designator, but there is only one F-16 AESA radar program and only one contract for it. Unlike record 17 on the same contract, this modification obligates RDT&E alone ('fiscal 2022 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $8,624,197') and the stated purpose is 'continued radar development', so the work belongs to the RDT&E F-16 line 0207133F (doc 412, RDT&E Air Force), whose own narrative owns APG-83 — not to the Aircraft Procurement AESA rows at F01600/F0160P. 'APG-83' appears at no other pe_bli in this index.

refute_a.reason: The obligation is RDT&E only ($8,624,197 fiscal 2022) for work the announcement calls 'continued radar development', and 0207133F's account is RDT&E, Air Force — the O&M-or-procurement-on-an-RDT&E-line failure mode is absent; the matched name is the APG-83 radar the PE's own narrative owns, not the F-16 platform, and 'F-16 Squadrons' is an operational development PE, not a catch-all title.

refute_b.reason: The announcement never says 'APG-83' — its actual words, 'Active Electronically Scanned Array radars of Air Force F-16 aircraft', are an EXACT-name match for two other index rows (F01600 and F0160P, both doc 407), so the quoted evidence links at least equally well elsewhere and in fact is used in this chunk (record 17) to link F01600 on the same contract; the APG-83 identification is an outside-knowledge inference that the announcement text does not carry.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for an engineering change proposal modification for the F-15 Passive/Active Warning and Survivability System (EPAWSS)
proposals.lexicon_quote: Eagle Passive/Active Warning Survivability System (EPAWSS) | 0207171F | 412 | F-15 EPAWSS
proposals.rationale: The announcement spells the program out and carries the acronym EPAWSS verbatim; the only difference from the index name is that the announcement writes 'F-15' where the J-book writes 'Eagle', which is the same aircraft. The action is an engineering change proposal — development work — funded entirely by 'fiscal 2022 and 2023 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $18,108,802', which matches 0207171F at doc 412 (RDT&E Air Force), the dedicated F-15 EPAWSS program element. Flagged for lens B: EPAWSS also appears under the procurement rows F015EX (F-15EX) and F15EWS (F-15 EPAW), both doc 407; the RDT&E-only obligation and the ECP nature of the action are what select the RDT&E line here.

refute_a.reason: An engineering change proposal funded entirely by fiscal 2022/2023 RDT&E ($18,108,802) against 0207171F, whose account is RDT&E, Air Force and whose title is literally 'F-15 EPAWSS' — appropriation, work type and program identity coincide, the program is the named thing rather than the F-15 platform, and the line is dedicated, not a rollup.

refute_b.reason: Three index rows own the EPAWSS name — 0207171F (doc 412), F015EX (doc 407) and F15EWS (doc 407, 'The F-15 Eagle Passive Active Warning Survivability System (EPAWSS)') — and the announcement's own phrasing 'F-15 Passive/Active Warning and Survivability System (EPAWSS)' matches the F15EWS row's F-15-prefixed name at least as closely as the Eagle-prefixed 0207171F row, so the name evidence cannot select an owner and the choice rests on appropriation reasoning rather than identity.
